What Is Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management?

Every Financial Step Between a Patient Walking In and a Claim Being Paid

Revenue cycle management, or RCM, is the complete financial process a practice runs on every patient it sees. It starts before the appointment, with eligibility verification and prior authorization, continues through charge capture and coding during the visit, and ends only once a claim is fully adjudicated and every dollar owed, from the payer and from the patient, has been collected.

Medical billing is one part of RCM. It is the middle of the cycle: turning a coded encounter into a submitted claim. RCM is the whole system around it, including the front-end steps that determine whether a claim will be clean in the first place, and the back-end steps that determine whether a patient balance actually gets collected.

Managing a practice's finances is genuinely complex. Payer rules change constantly, documentation standards tighten, and patients now carry more financial responsibility than ever through high-deductible health plans. PMEX's RCM service aligns every stage of that cycle, front-end, mid-cycle and back-end, so revenue actually reaches the practice instead of leaking out at the seams.

Our Revenue Cycle Workflow

Front-End, Mid-Cycle and Back-End, Working as One System

Most RCM breakdowns happen at the handoff between stages: front-end skips a step and mid-cycle inherits a bad claim, or mid-cycle submits clean but back-end never follows up on the balance. PMEX runs all three stages under one team and one dashboard, so nothing is handed off and forgotten.

Front-End RCM

Before the Visit

  • Patient registration and demographic capture
  • Insurance eligibility and benefits verification
  • Prior authorization coordination
  • Patient cost-share estimation before service

Mid-Cycle RCM

During and Right After the Visit

  • Charge capture from encounter documentation
  • Compliant ICD-10/CPT coding
  • Claim creation, scrubbing and validation
  • Clean-claim submission and status tracking

Back-End RCM

After Adjudication

  • Remittance processing and payment posting
  • Denial management and payer follow-up
  • A/R management and aging recovery
  • Patient statements and collections

RCM KPIs We Monitor

The Metrics That Actually Predict Financial Health

These are the same KPIs a CFO would want on a dashboard, tracked continuously instead of compiled once a quarter.

Days in A/R (DAR)

The average number of days it takes to collect payment from payers and patients after a claim is filed.

Claim Acceptance Rate

The share of claims accepted by payers on the first submission, with no errors or rejections.

Denial Rate

The share of claims denied by payers, broken down by reason so patterns get fixed at the source.

Collection Rate

The percentage of total billed amount actually collected from payers and patients combined.

Net Collection Ratio

The percentage of the payer-allowed amount that is actually collected, the truest measure of performance.

A/R Aging Distribution

Outstanding balances broken into 30/60/90/120-plus day buckets, so old claims get priority before they age out.

Revenue Cycle Management: Frequently Asked Questions

RCM is the process of managing the financial side of a practice's operations. It covers patient registration, eligibility verification, coding, billing, claims, and collecting and reconciling payments from patients and payers.

Billing alone only manages claim submission. RCM also covers eligibility verification before the visit and patient collections after it, the two stages most likely to cause a clean claim to still go unpaid.

Every denial and rejection reason is monitored and analyzed, then corrected and resubmitted as quickly as possible. We follow up with payers directly and negotiate on the practice's behalf, and keep the practice informed of status until resolution.

We track days in A/R, claim acceptance rate, denial rate, collection rate and net collection ratio, and make every one of them visible on the PMEX dashboard in real time.

All RCM workflows comply with HIPAA and run on encrypted, access-controlled systems, protecting patient and financial data from unauthorized access at every stage of the cycle.

Yes. PMEX works with the EHR and practice management system your practice already uses, so no migration or system replacement is required to start.
